html:
The Tale of Kiều is a long Vietnamese poem by Nguyễn Du, written in the early 1800s. It is the most famous work of Vietnamese literature, and many Vietnamese can recite long passages of it.

It retells a Chinese prose novel of the late Ming or early Qing period in 3,254 lines of lục bát, the native six and eight syllable verse form. Thúy Kiều, a beautiful and gifted young woman, sells herself to save her father and brother from prison. She is forced into prostitution and endures fifteen years of suffering before she is reunited with her family and her first love.

It was written in chữ Nôm, the script for writing Vietnamese with Chinese based characters, which showed that Vietnamese itself could carry great poetry. Later it was printed in the Vietnamese alphabet and became even more widely read. Its lines entered proverbs and everyday speech, people used it to tell fortunes by opening it at random, and readers took Kiều's sacrifice as a symbol of the suffering of Vietnam.
sum: The Tale of Kiều is a long Vietnamese poem by Nguyễn Du, written in the early 1800s. It is the most famous work of Vietnamese literature, and many Vietnamese can recite long passages of it.
